headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from Copilot-to-marker document handoff; no shared write channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot can read repo context and open editor buffers, while marker has no documented ingestion channel or shared workspace. The pair lacks a proven automatic bridge, so prompt injection is not default-path dangerous; any risk would require manual copy/paste or an undocumented integration.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Copilot output into marker input
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Avoid copy/pasting raw model output into marker
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue
Review copied text before passing it to marker

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, but marker is documented as not reading files or using network egress. With no shared filesystem or authenticated workspace overlap shown, leakage is limited to manual transfer of content rather than default exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive repository or document set
IF an operator exports Copilot context into marker inputs
mitigations: Do not feed secrets into Copilot buffers
Redact sensitive passages before document processing
Confirm marker is not given repo-wide exports

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write files and modify git state, while marker cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. The overlap is asymmetric and does not create a default write-write conflict; the main risk is operator confusion if Copilot edits files that marker later consumes.
conditions: IF marker is extended to write back into the same repository
IF Copilot Workspace edits are auto-applied while marker is simultaneously generating derived files
mitigations: Require human review before applying Copilot edits
Keep marker outputs in a separate directory
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use git status checks before merging outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace plans and applies edits for human review, and marker is a document-processing tool that could be used to transform Copilot-produced text. If marker consumes Copilot output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade across multiple work products even though neither profile proves autonomous action-taking.
conditions: IF marker is fed Copilot-generated text as source material
IF the operator accepts marker output without checking against the original document
mitigations: Verify marker output against the source document
Keep Copilot drafts clearly labeled as untrusted
Add a manual review step before downstream use
Compare extracted facts to the original file

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for this pair. Copilot is closed-source and marker is open-source, but the rubric’s compliance risks require a concrete policy mismatch, which is absent here.
conditions: IF a deployment policy assigns regulated data to one agent but not the other
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced that differs between the two
mitigations: Document data-handling policy for both tools
Keep regulated data out of both tools until policy is confirmed
